# Taste

Curated by Skill Harbor: a creative-direction layer for music videos and short-form edits, the "what and why" above the mechanics. It encodes a specific, opinionated taste (the angelcore / cloud-trance / hyperpop family) as an actionable system: a named-genre aesthetic vocabulary drawn from a ~70-entry visual library, a concrete mood, palette, light, and texture system, a beat-synced editing grammar (beat-locked hard cuts, hero-on-black macro inserts, bloom reveals, color-pop on monochrome, speed ramps into the drop), and a pipeline chaining the ECC video skills from b-roll generation to distribution. The core thesis: decide the genre before the first generation, because coherence beats novelty, and taste decided last means every upstream render was a guess. Pure Markdown skill. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: deliberately opinionated about one aesthetic family; adapt the vocabulary section if your project lives elsewhere. It directs; rendering and cutting happen in video-editing, remotion-video-creation, and fal-ai-media. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
